title: Ember Watch retro and open actions — 2028-09-21
content:
Shift window: 21:00 UTC 2028-09-21 -> 05:00 UTC 2028-09-22
Owner: Priya Menon (night primary)
Bucket: Ember Watch (EMB-region routing)

Summary (high level)
- Quiet first three hours. Small spike in 95/99 latency around 01:12 UTC attributed to a scheduled cache compaction on dedicated pool (see events below).
- One customer-facing incident (INC-4829) with partial throttling on embedding generation between 01:10–01:34 UTC. Root cause appears to be simultaneous background compaction + degraded NVMe queueing on ded-capacity-03.
- Multiple minor alerts (4) for kube-probe flaps across autoscaled workers; all recovered automatically or by PM restarts.
- No primary region failover; no paging to on-call escalation beyond L2.

Incidents and timeline
- 00:58 UTC: Pager — p99 > 1.2s for embedding endpoints (alert EMB-P99-LAT). Investigated: small concurrent increase in batch sizes from a downstream consumer (internal qa-runner).
- 01:06 UTC: Degraded IO metrics on ded-capacity-03 node (high iowait). Kube-level pod restarts started happening ~01:08.
- 01:10 UTC: INC-4829 opened by alert rule auto-create. Customer reports timeouts on embedding requests.
- 01:12 UTC: Noted cache compaction job (scheduled nightly) kicked off across the dedicated pool. This job holds exclusive locks on certain prefix caches for ~20–40s per shard.
- 01:14 UTC: Manual throttling rule applied to non-critical QA consumer to reduce burst. Reduced incoming QPS by ~40%.
- 01:22 UTC: detour: NVMe queue depth hit saturation on ded-capacity-03; engineer Liam O'Connor started node inspection and moved hot pods to spare instances (live migration via k8s drain + pod reschedule).
- 01:34 UTC: Observed p99 latency returns to baseline. INC-4829 marked as mitigated.
- 02:10 UTC: Two kube-probe flaps on worker pool emb-wk-2; auto-restarted by k8s, tickets opened for follow-up to avoid noisy alerts.

Actions taken (on-call)
- Applied immediate rate-limiting to the internal qa-runner (Slack: @qa-bot).
- Drained ded-capacity-03 and cordoned for deeper inspection. Created ticket SRE-1372 for hardware-level NVMe telemetry review and replacement planning.
- Temporarily increased cache compaction window jitter to reduce synchronized compactions (patch applied to ember-compactor config: jitter_seed=0.33).
- Notified product on-call for customer INC-4829 with summary and status.

Outstanding follow-ups (owners + ETA)
- SRE-1372 (Liam O'Connor) — NVMe SMART telemetry extraction and vendor support engage. ETA: 2028-09-27.
- Runbook edit: ember-watch-runbook-v2 (Priya Menon) — add explicit step: pre-check NVMe queue depth before running compaction; add backoff policy. ETA: 2028-09-24.
- Reduce noisey kube-probe alerts (Yuki Sato) — change probe thresholds for emb-wk pools; test in canary. ETA: 2028-09-23.
- Customer outreach (CS) for INC-4829 (Daniel Kim) — draft apology + impact summary. ETA: 2028-09-22.

Runbook notes and proposed edits (quick diff)
- Current compaction step: run compactor across shards sequentially.
- Proposed change: add preflight check: if node iowait > 15% OR NVMe queue_depth > 85% then abort compaction and schedule jittered retry (backoff x2, max 3 attempts).
- Add step to temporarily rate limit known high-volume internal consumers (QA, benchmarking) during compaction windows — provide sample kubectl command and Grafana panel link for immediate action.
- Add clear escalation rung: if p99 > 1.0s for > 5m AND node iowait > 10% -> page L2 + run "drain-fast" playbook (doc link included in runbook).

Metrics snapshot (peak values during window)
- p95 embedding latency: 420ms (baseline ~180ms)
- p99 embedding latency: 1.35s (baseline ~520ms)
- Error rate (5m): 2.6% (spike from timeouts during NVMe saturation)
- ded-capacity-03 iowait: peaked 48%
- NVMe queue depth: peaked at 92%

Pager/alert noise and tuning suggestions
- EMB-PROBE-FLAP: noisy alert for emb-wk probes — consider increasing failure threshold from 3 -> 6 and probe timeout from 1s -> 2s for emb worker pools (low-risk).
- EMB-P99-LAT: consider adding a companion alert that suppresses pages when known maintenance window flag = true (we have maintenance metadata in alerts).

Checklist for next shift (short and actionable)
- Check SRE-1372 status and update on node replacement timeline.
- Confirm compactor jitter value persisted across deploys (config git ref: github.com/redwood/ember-compactor @r3f9c4).
- Validate that QA consumer rate-limits are still applied; release them if no regression.
- Run smoke query against embeddings for 5m at 10qps and confirm p99 < 700ms.
- Review any new kube-probe flaps and escalate if pattern repeats.

Contacts and escalation matrix (for this shift)
- L1: on-duty SRE (this doc owner) — Priya Menon — pager/email/Slack DM
- L2: Liam O'Connor — storage and node remediation
- Product on-call: Daniel Kim — customer comms
- Infra lead: Yuki Sato — kube-probe alert tuning

Notes to self / informal observations
- The compaction job is effective for long-term cache health but is brittle on older NVMe nodes — vendor agreed to ship replacements if SMART shows wear.
- Consider temporarily moving night compaction to lower-traffic windows in APAC-only region to avoid overlapping with EU/NA peaks during late-night stress tests.
- Keep an eye on internal benchmarking cluster; it often spikes at 00:45 UTC and collides with maintenance windows. Add it to the runbook preflight check list.

Appendix: quick commands used
- rate-limit QA consumer: kubectl patch cronjob qa-runner -p '{\"spec\":{\"suspend\":true}}' -n internal
- drain node gracefully: kubectl cordon ded-capacity-03 && kubectl drain ded-capacity-03 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
- compactor config check: curl -s https://config.redwood.internal/ember-compactor | jq '.compaction.jitter'

End of shift handover — handing over to morning primary (Ava Thompson).

---
Draft status: needs review for runbook wording and confirmation of SRE-1372 timeline.

Comments welcome in-line or on Slack #ops-ember-watch.
